statement: Let O(n)=floor(n^(3/2)), P>=256, 1<=h<=P/2 an integer, and n<n' odd integers in (P,2P]. Set beta_h(n)=O(n+2h)-O(n) and G_h(n)=O(O(n+2h))-O(O(n)). If beta_h(n)=beta_h(n'), then G_h(n')-G_h(n)>h*(n'-n)*P^(1/4)/2-2>=2, hence this integer difference is at least 3. The corresponding floor of the real increment O(n+2h)^(3/2)-O(n)^(3/2) also strictly increases between these points. A positive mixed derivative and a floor loss strictly below two prove the statement uniformly. This rules out freezing the next gap on an actual first-gap branch containing two odd sources; it does not assert monotonicity across different first gaps or refute cancellation of K3. Elementary written strengthening of the existing method obstruction; independent review and Lean verification outstanding.

Define oddMap(n)=Nat.sqrt(n^3), oddChain(d,n) by requiring all d+1 formal odd iterates to be odd, ancestors(d,m) as the natural n<=m with oddChain(d,n) and iterate(oddMap,d,n)=m, and weight(d,m) as their finite cardinality. The map is strictly increasing and at least n. oddChain(d,n) is equivalent to follows(n,replicate(d+1,odd)), and on it iterate(floorPower,d,n)=iterate(oddMap,d,n). Each weight is at most one and is zero at even m. For any naturals d,B, finite I with every m in I at most B, and g:Nat -> Complex, sum_{m in I} weight(d,m)*g(m) equals sum g(iterate(oddMap,d,n)) over n<=B with oddChain(d,n) and iterate(oddMap,d,n) in I. For positive n, putting m=oddMap(oddMap(n)) gives m^4<=n^9<64*(m+1)^4; the unrestricted inverse image of an integer interval is order-convex. The rational exponent budgets in OddPredecessorTransport.lean hold. These exact statements are kernel-checked; the ledger label awaits advisory coverage. No analytic estimate or all-depth pressure bound is claimed as a Lean result.

Inherited corollary of the written Paper B Theorem 4.11, with its independent analytic review outstanding. Let O(n)=floor(n^(3/2)) and b_d(m) count natural n such that O^d(n)=m and all d+1 states are odd. For every epsilon>0, uniformly for real M>=2, intervals I contained in (M,2M], and nonzero integer h, the sum W_2,h(I)=sum_{m in I} b_2(m)*exp(2*pi*i*h*m^(3/2)/2) is O_epsilon(M^(127/288+epsilon)+abs(h)^24). In particular abs(h)<=M^(1/60) gives error O_epsilon(M^(4/9-1/288+epsilon)). Similarly W_1,h(I) is O_epsilon(M^(127/192+epsilon)+abs(h)^24), with the tail absorbed for abs(h)<=M^(1/40). The proof pulls back to the exact guarded original-source interval, uses Paper B modes (i,j,h,0) or (i,h,0,0), and keeps the frequency-dependent dyadic tail when passing to prefixes. It does not smooth either odd predecessor, assume a short-interval theorem, or prove the fourth odd phase or growing-depth pressure. This is a consolidation of an existing theorem, not a new independent exponential-sum proof.
